memory_candidates.content: When re-pointing a derived claim's proof from an unconditional theorem instance to a conditional one indexed over a finite set (e.g. certified past-types pt subset of a fixed finite literal set), write the re-derivation as: (1) the per-index instance follows from the conditional theorem by stripping any extra necessitation modality (reflexivity, phi -> box phi -> phi), (2) close the finite conjunction over the index set explicitly rather than asserting it, citing the finiteness fact by name (e.g. 'PastLits is finite'). This keeps a re-pointing proof auditable against the exact theorem it now cites, rather than leaving the reader to reconstruct why the new citation suffices.
